issues.text: The lesson's own test is "wrap when a rule belongs to the value", and "never negative" is the rule it gives for a price. A product's stored price is also a price, so the same rule seems to belong to it, yet it stays `int` with no reason given. I cannot tell whether this is a deliberate choice, a cost trade-off, or just not done yet, so I doubt I understood the test.
issues.quote: the stored `Product.PriceVnd` and payment amounts stay `int`.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this clause saying why they stay `int` here (e.g. they are outside what this module changes, so the rule is not yet enforced for them), so the reader does not read it as contradicting the test.

issues.text: The text says the private setter lets an item swap in a different `Vnd`, but never says when or why an item would do that. Since nothing in the lesson changes a unit price, I wondered why the setter exists at all instead of `{ get; }`.
issues.quote: That private setter lets an item swap in a different `Vnd` object; it can never change the amount inside a `Vnd`, which has no setter at all.
issues.fix: Add half a sentence saying what the private setter is there for, or say plainly that the lesson does not use it and the point is only that it cannot reach inside a `Vnd`.

issues.text: The last paragraph of section 5 holds the rule for wrapping, the counter-view about ids, how Đơn Hàng turns a product price into a `Vnd`, what stays `int`, and why `Quantity` stays `int`. I re-read it twice; "the opposite view" and "the narrow path" made me stop to work out which view each was opposite to.
issues.quote: Some teams take the opposite view and wrap values with no rule at all, such as ids
issues.fix: Split before "Đơn Hàng takes the narrow path": one paragraph for when wrapping pays off (both views), one for what Đơn Hàng wraps and what stays `int`.

issues.text: q5: option b gives only one reason, the shared `Vnd.Zero`, and option c removes exactly that reason. From the text I could not decide between b and c; the deciding idea (a value object never changes, so any holder is safe) is only in the explanation of c, not in b itself.
issues.quote: Keep `Vnd` as it is: changing amounts in place would break the shared `Vnd.Zero`.
issues.fix: Reword b to lead with the principle, e.g. "Keep `Vnd` as it is: a `Vnd` that can change in place is no longer a value object, and the shared `Vnd.Zero` would be the first thing it breaks."

issues.text: q3, explanation of e: "value type" is not in what I know and the lesson never uses it, so the explanation of a wrong option brings in a new term just when I am trying to see why I was wrong.
issues.quote: Comparing by value sounds like something a value type would do, so a struct seems implied.
issues.fix: Replace "something a value type would do" with "something a struct would do".

issues.text: q4: the line with the blank is the `Times` line from the `Vnd` code block, identical except for the blank, so I can copy `new` from the block without understanding why a new object keeps the unit price unchanged.
issues.fix: Blank a line not shown verbatim in the lesson, e.g. ask for the start of a `Minus` method written the same way, or ask what `Times` returns instead of blanking the code.
